transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, I'm here because my sleep has basically just fallen apart lately. I'll lie in bed in my apartment for hours, you know, laptop closed, but I'm still mentally rechecking everything. Work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments... it just doesn't stop. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off.
Do these worries also occupy your mind during the day, when you are not trying to sleep?

Yeah, they definitely do. It's pretty much all day long. My mind just keeps jumping around from one thing to another. Like, I'll be worrying about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then it immediately shifts to whether I'm wasting my money on school, or... or if my family is going to think I just can't handle things. It basically feels like I treat every small issue that comes up like it could completely derail my whole future.
How long have you been worrying this much, nearly every day?
It's been... probably about a year and three months now. It really started right around the time I began an evening graduate certificate program, on top of keeping my full-time analyst job.
When your work or school demands are temporarily lighter, does the worrying still continue at about the same level?

Um... I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't actually had a time where things were lighter since I started the program. Between the analyst job and the evening classes, it's just been a constant stream of deadlines. So, yeah, I haven't really had the chance to see if the worrying would drop off or not.
Before you started the graduate program, did you already have this kind of excessive worry?

No, not like this. I mean, I'd get stressed out sometimes if I had a big presentation at work or something like that, but... it was normal stress, you know? Once the presentation was over, I'd feel fine again. It wasn't this constant, all-day thing where my brain just won't shut off. This level of worrying is definitely new since I took on the extra classes.
When your mind feels relatively calm, do you still have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

I don't really know, to be honest. My mind hasn't really felt calm in over a year, so I haven't had a chance to see if I'd sleep better without the worrying. Right now, I definitely have trouble with sleep, but I don't know what it would be like if my mind were actually quiet.
When you compare your worries with what is objectively happening at work and school, do they feel excessive or out of proportion to the actual demands?

Yes, I think they probably are. I mean, my mind just keeps jumping from one thing to another. I worry about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then I start stressing about whether I'm just wasting money on school. Then I worry about whether my family thinks I can't handle it all. It's like... I treat every small issue like it could completely derail my whole future. So, objectively, yeah, it's probably out of proportion to what's actually happening.
Do you worry excessively about areas of your life that are unrelated to your job or graduate program?

No, not really. It's pretty much just focused on work and school, and how those two things affect everything else. I mean, I worry about my family's opinion, like I said, but that's still tied back to whether I can handle my job and my classes. I don't really sit around worrying about my health or the news or... things like that. It's all just centered on the pressure from work and the graduate program.
Which started first: the persistent worrying or the difficulty sleeping?

I'm honestly not sure which one started first. It all kind of blurs together at this point. I just know it's been going on for over a year now, but I couldn't tell you if the worrying caused the bad sleep first, or if I started sleeping poorly and then the worrying got worse. It feels like they both just kind of showed up around the same time.
What troubles you more overall: the persistent worry itself, or the difficulty sleeping?

I don't know, it's hard to separate them. I guess... probably the worry itself. The lack of sleep is awful, don't get me wrong, it makes everything harder. But the worrying is just so constant and overwhelming. It's what keeps me awake in the first place, and it's what's running through my head all day. So yeah, I'd say the worry is the bigger problem.
